subject: Post-demo: runtime-ready model slate + integration risks
messages:
From: marissa.co@redwood.com
To: Chris Barnes <chris@finview.ai>, Ava Lim <ava.lim@finview.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-20 10:15 PDT
Subject: Post-demo: runtime-ready model slate + integration risks

Hi Chris / Ava —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Below is a concise post-call synthesis with recommended next steps for an MVP integration and the three model options we think are runtime-ready for FinView's use case (real-time transaction summarization + fraud flagging). I focused on tradeoffs you'll care about: latency, cost (per-1M tokens), and quality on your sample prompt set.

Executive shortlist (rationale in-line):

1) Redwood-OPT-13B (quantized FP16) — Balanced latency & quality
   - Latency: ~120ms per token p95 on Dedicated T4 pool
   - Cost: mid-range; good throughput with batching
   - Why: Strong on short-form summarization and hallucination resistance for your financial templates. Lowest integration friction (same tokenizer, no architecture changes).

2) OpenLlama-30B (INT8 + KV-cache warmups) — Higher quality, more variable latency
   - Latency: ~220-300ms/token p95 depending on sequence length
   - Cost: ~1.6x Redwood-OPT-13B per token
   - Why: Best raw QA and nuanced contextual recall on your 50-example eval. We'll recommend aggressive prefix caching to keep SLOs acceptable.

3) Redwood-CLIP-7B-LLM (retrained compact) — Low cost, fastest p50 latency but lower edge-case fidelity
   - Latency: ~70ms/token p50, p95 ~140ms
   - Cost: lowest; targeted for high throughput endpoints with deterministic prompts
   - Why: Good for bulk classification/routing (flagging) where recall > generative finesse. Consider as a secondary tier for pre-filtering.

Quality/regression concerns:
- The demo prompt set exposed a few hallucination patterns for longer multi-sentence summaries. We recommend a small regression harness (10–20 golden prompts) that runs on every model rollout.
- Temperature and stop-sequence control are critical; we'll supply a locked prompt template and a guardrail evaluation that flags regressions >6% on precision for the fraud flag task.

Benchmarks & deliverables attached: prompt pack (finview_prompt_pack_v1.zip) + benchmark csv (finview_benchmarks_v2.csv). Links: HubSpot deal (see link below) and shared Drive containing eval scripts.

Next steps (proposal):
- FinView: confirm which model(s) you want in the MVP slate (pick 1 primary + 1 fallback) by EOD Thur 4/26.
- Redwood: run a focused p95 latency sweep with your real-cardinality prompts and send updated cost estimate (we'll complete by Mon 4/22).
- Set up a 45m integration sync (engineering + security) week of 4/29 to review network/KMS and data retention.

If helpful I've assigned Kar thik to lead the benchmark follow-ups and Soojin to own the integration checklist.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwood.com

Attachments: finview_prompt_pack_v1.zip (37 files), finview_benchmarks_v2.csv (benchmarks summary)
From: Chris Barnes <chris@finview.ai>

Cc: Ava Lim <ava.lim@finview.ai>
Date: 2028-04-20 14:32 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo: runtime-ready model slate + integration risks

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side before we confirm:

1) For Redwood-OPT-13B, can you confirm tokenization parity with our current pipeline (we use byte-level BPE)? Any re-tokenization risk for our archived data?
2) For OpenLlama-30B, the p95 you listed looks borderline for some of our real-time widgets (SLO 350ms). With prefix caching, do you have a realistic plan to keep p95 under 350ms for sequences <1k tokens?
3) How disruptive is integrating a two-tier runtime (primary + prefilter model) for feature flags? We want to avoid doubling engineering complexity.

We'll review attachments and get back to you today on preferred slate.

—Chris
Chief Product Officer, FinView
chris@finview.ai
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Chris Barnes <chris@finview.ai>, marissa.co@redwood.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-21 09:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo: runtime-ready model slate + integration risks

Thanks Chris — short answers (more detail in Drive link):

1) Tokenization: Redwood-OPT-13B uses standard byte-level BPE (same family). We ran a compatibility pass on a 2M-row sample of your archived outputs and saw <0.4% rare-token re-encoding differences. No re-tokenization of archives required; just map at ingest if you want exact byte parity.

2) OpenLlama-30B latency: With KV prefix caching + throughput-aware batching on Dedicated, we observed median p95 ~280ms on our test harness for sequences under 1k tokens. If you run on Dedicated with our T4-optimized kernel and enable adaptive small-batch routing, keeping p95 under 350ms is realistic. We'll provide the raw sweep CSV in the Drive folder.

3) Two-tier runtime complexity: our recommendation is to implement the prefilter model (Redwood-CLIP-7B-LLM) as a sidecar route that runs asynchronously for high-volume streams. It can be introduced behind a feature flag with ~3 ACC engineering-days for the integration (routing + metrics + rollout policy). We can scope an SOW if you want a dedicated integration sprint.

I've dropped the exact benchmark CSV and the latency-sweep scripts in the shared folder: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1FvFinviewBenchmarks

Karthik
Sr. ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Chris / Ava —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary / ask before the 4/26 internal decision:

- If you prioritize latency headroom and consistent p95, pick Redwood-OPT-13B as primary and OpenLlama-30B as fallback for high-fidelity queries.
- If cost and throughput are primary (high-volume classification + lower generative fidelity), pick Redwood-CLIP-7B-LLM as primary with Redwood-OPT-13B as fallback.

Concrete asks:
1) Please reply to this thread with the primary+fallback choice by EOD 2028-04-26.
2) Share the security contact for the 4/30 sync (name + email).

We've attached a short integration SOW stub (MVP_integration_checklist.pdf) and the benchmarks + prompt pack — let us know if you'd like us to pre-populate a canary rollout policy for you.

If it's helpful, we can also run a 48-hour guided pilot with a capped request budget to validate p95 and quality on your production-like traffic.

Best —
